finding: The instantaneous recruitment response to rooted-stock removal is hump-shaped rather than monotonic. Modest partial reductions consistently increase recruitment hazard, while complete removal reduces it.
mechanism_interpretation: Partial stock removal increases the eligible fraction of represented population while fielded formations, foothold strength, social exposure, capital, grievance, fear, and political access remain fixed.
The decline at complete removal shows that eligibility alone is not sufficient: member/rootedness-related access also contributes to recruitment intensity.

Pineland therefore contains a compensatory-recruitment window in which thinning an underground can increase replacement pressure before sufficiently deep destruction removes enough organizational access to reverse the effect.
limits: This is a partial-equilibrium day-60 diagnostic, not a realistic intervention.
The shocked state deliberately leaves downstream access variables frozen, so it identifies arithmetic/mechanistic pressure rather than a full dynamic causal effect.
The exact location of the peak is not identified by the preregistered six-point grid and should be mapped on fresh seeds before making a threshold claim.
next_question: Does the same hump-shaped replacement-pressure mechanism predict actual recruited mass and rebound under dynamic temporary disruption?
guard: Synthetic Pineland mechanism only; no real-world operational prescription.
